scientific_question: On the untouched NIST Gauss1 smooth generated dataset, can the reusable external coverage driver evaluate a cubic/cubic candidate, continuous ellipsoid safety and pointwise residual coverage without protocol drift?

dataset_scope.name: NIST/ITL StRD Gauss1
dataset_scope.native_model: Eight-parameter exponential class: two well-separated Gaussians on a decaying exponential baseline; the cubic/cubic rational candidate is an approximation stress test, not the native model
dataset_scope.noise_model: Normally distributed zero-mean noise with variance 6.25, as stated by NIST; descriptive source metadata, not a substitute for deterministic residual bounds

implementation_rule.driver_changes_after_freeze: Not permitted under this protocol; any driver change requires a new protocol and preservation of this frozen analysis

candidate_rule.optimizer: scipy.optimize.curve_fit method=lm, maxfev=200000, full_output=true; select lowest training RSS
candidate_rule.retuning: No model, start, radius, fold or threshold changes after seeing outcomes

fold_rule.construction: Sort unique x values into five contiguous, nearly equal groups; repeated x never crosses fitting and test sets; every observation is evaluated once
fold_rule.baseline: Cubic polynomial fitted only on the other four groups; this is a candidate baseline, not the native eight-parameter exponential fit

ellipsoid_rule.radius_scope: Fixed before fitting; a deterministic scale only, not a confidence level
ellipsoid_rule.covariance: Use denominator block from the best training attempt; require exact symmetry and positive definiteness
ellipsoid_rule.continuous_certificate: Require exact D^2-rho^2*z^T*Sigma*z>0 and sign-consistent D over each closed held-out interval
ellipsoid_rule.pointwise_bound: For R=rho*sqrt_upper(z^T Sigma z), require |D|-R>0 and compute prediction shift and observed residual upper bounds; compare with the independent box at the same radius
ellipsoid_rule.coverage: Check actual |y-f_snapshot| against each available deterministic residual bound and record any violation; do not call this probability calibration

prohibitions: No claim that the native Gauss1 model is cubic/cubic or that the candidate is physically endogenous
No description of generated observations as an independent physical experiment
No hiding of optimizer failures, non-positive covariance, unavailable bounds or coverage violations
No probability, confidence, RMSE-bound or continuous-x error-bound claim from pointwise bounds
No use of the original eight-parameter certified fit as candidate holdout evidence
No retuning of starts, radius, folds or candidate degree after seeing candidate outcomes
